title: Breathing and Gas Exchange
seo_title: Year 8 Science: Breathing and Gas Exchange Worksheets (Lungs, Alveoli, Diaphragm)
standard_text: The structure and functions of the gas exchange system in humans, including adaptations to function; the mechanism of breathing to move air in and out of the lungs, using a pressure model to explain the movement of gases, including simple measurements of lung volume; the impact of exercise, asthma and smoking on the human gas exchange system; the role of leaf stomata in gas exchange in plants.
meta_desc: Free Year 8 science worksheets on breathing and gas exchange: the lungs, alveoli, the diaphragm, inhaled and exhaled air, exercise, asthma and smoking. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Gas exchange happens in the alveoli.
key_sub: Breathing in: the diaphragm contracts, chest volume rises, pressure falls.
body_html:
How to think about it

Breathing moves air in and out; gas exchange happens in the alveoli.

  • Air path: nose or mouth → trachea → bronchi → bronchioles → alveoli.
  • Breathing in: diaphragm and intercostal muscles contract, ribs move up and out, chest volume increases, pressure falls, air flows in.
  • In the alveoli, oxygen diffuses into the blood and carbon dioxide diffuses out.
Example

Breathing in: what does the diaphragm do?

It contracts

Answer: flattens and moves down

Example

Oxygen: 21% inhaled, 16% exhaled. Difference?

21 − 16

Answer: 5 percentage points

Common mistakes

  • Thinking the lungs suck air in by themselves.
  • Thinking we breathe out only carbon dioxide.
  • Mixing up breathing and respiration.

faq.q: What happens when you breathe in?
faq.a: The diaphragm contracts and flattens and the intercostal muscles pull the ribs up and out. The chest volume increases, the pressure falls and air flows into the lungs.

faq.q: Why are alveoli good at gas exchange?
faq.a: They have a huge surface area, walls one cell thick, a moist lining and a rich blood supply, so gases diffuse quickly.

faq.q: How is exhaled air different from inhaled air?
faq.a: It has less oxygen (about 16% instead of 21%), much more carbon dioxide (about 4% instead of 0.04%) and more water vapour.

items.q: Evie writes in a health journal: “You run a race and breathe hard.” Which two body systems work together most here?
items.e: The lungs take in more oxygen, and the heart pumps faster to carry it to the muscles.

items.q: Aisha writes in a health journal: “You lift a heavy backpack.” Which two body systems work together most here?
items.e: Muscles pull on bones to lift the bag.

items.q: Ethan asks: what is the main job of the excretory system?
c: It removes wastes from the body.
It moves blood that carries oxygen and nutrients to every cell.
It takes in oxygen and gets rid of carbon dioxide.
It collects information and sends messages that control the body.
items.e: The excretory system removes wastes from the body.

items.q: Maya writes in a health journal: “You exercise and start to sweat.” Which two body systems work together most here?
